title: Aurora marketplace index (v1)
description: The composed, signed catalogue Aurora fetches at runtime. Produced by marketplace/scripts/compose.py from the per-package manifests, and validated in CI before signing. See docs/MARKETPLACE_HOSTING_PLAN.md.

schema_version.description: The marketplace index schema this blob was written against. Aurora refuses to load an index whose schema_version is newer than it knows how to parse.

index_version.description: Monotonic catalogue version, e.g. v2026.08.28-a3f2c1 (date + short content hash). Aurora keys its 'new catalogue available' notice on a change here.

generated_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp the index was composed.

min_dashboard_version.description: The oldest dashboard build that can parse this index. Aurora refuses (with a 'your dashboard needs an update' banner) and falls back to its last compatible cached index if its own version is older.

slug.description: Canonical name and URL key. Same as the package directory name.

icon.description: Bundled-icon slug, resolved by the dashboard to /icons/<slug>.svg.

requires.description: The manifest requires block (min_ram_mb, min_disk_gb, start_budget_seconds, host_roles).

images.description: Every container image this app runs, pinned by digest. Tag-only entries are rejected: a catalogue that cannot pin an image cannot promise every box the same bytes. When a compose image reference carries only a tag, the composer records digest:null and the app is flagged unpinned so CI can warn without failing the whole catalogue.

ref.description: The image reference as written in compose (e.g. lscr.io/linuxserver/jellyfin:latest).

digest.description: The resolved image digest, or null when the composer could not resolve one (e.g. no registry access at compose time).

compose.description: The full compose.yml, embedded (open question 1, option 1: embedded for v1). Airgaps cleanly; the whole catalogue is one artifact.

env_example.description: The .env.example body, embedded. What each variable is for and its default.

unpinned.description: True when at least one image could not be pinned by digest at compose time. The dashboard surfaces this on the consent screen.
